evidenceAudit.scope: Generalised anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, agoraphobia and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in India: assessment, exclusion of physical causes, psychoeducation, escitalopram in primary care, second SSRI and CBT in secondary care, tertiary options and short-term benzodiazepine use, built on the ICMR Anxiety Disorders STW (October 2019).
findings: Disorder types, assessment items (duration, impairment, depression, substance use, thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, hypoglycaemia), escitalopram 5 mg then 10 mg then 20 mg, continuation 1–2 years after remission, second SSRI maxima (sertraline 200, fluoxetine 60, paroxetine 50, fluvoxamine 300 mg/day), diazepam 5–10 mg at night for up to 1 month with 2-week taper, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and referral levels checked against the ICMR Anxiety Disorders STW (October 2019).
unverifiedSections: Starting doses of second SSRIs are not given in the STW; only maximum doses are shown.
Tertiary drugs (clomipramine for OCD; venlafaxine, duloxetine, pregabalin, tricyclics) are named without doses in the STW and are left to specialist prescribing.
No screening tool or follow-up interval is named in the STW.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Anxiety disorders are the commonest mental disorders and often present in Indian primary care as physical complaints — palpitations, breathlessness, headache, abdominal symptoms — with repeated investigations. The ICMR workflow asks clinicians to identify the type of disorder, assess duration and impairment, look for depression, substance use and physical causes (thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, hypoglycaemia), give psychoeducation and start escitalopram. Benzodiazepines are only for short-term relief of severe anxiety. Non-responders move to a second SSRI and CBT at district level, and to tertiary care after that.
keyMechanisms: Over-activity of fear circuits (amygdala) with reduced prefrontal control.
Serotonin and noradrenaline systems modulate anxiety; SSRIs reduce symptoms over weeks.
Avoidance maintains anxiety by preventing new learning.
OCD involves cortico-striatal circuits; responds to SSRIs and exposure-based CBT.

symptoms: Chronic worry about everyday matters (GAD) (ICMR STW)
Sudden attacks of intense fear with physical symptoms (panic) (ICMR STW)
Fear and avoidance of social situations or leaving home (ICMR STW)
Unwanted thoughts and repetitive behaviours (OCD) (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Physical cause: thyrotoxicosis, phaeochromocytoma, hypoglycaemia (ICMR STW)
No improvement after escitalopram titration: refer (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Weight loss, tremor, goitre; low TSH.
Low mood and loss of interest predominate.

clinicalManagement.title: Primary care
actions: Psychoeducation and reassurance; reduce avoidance; explain OCD thoughts are part of the illness (ICMR STW).
Escitalopram 5 mg at night, 10 mg after 1 week, 20 mg after 4–6 weeks if needed (ICMR STW).
No improvement after a further 4–6 weeks: refer (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: District hospital
actions: Second SSRI for about 2–3 months; CBT if available (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Tertiary centre
actions: CBT preferred, alone or with medicine (ICMR STW).
Third SSRI or clomipramine for OCD; venlafaxine, duloxetine, pregabalin or tricyclics for other disorders; augmentation (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Continuation
actions: Continue escitalopram at least 1–2 years after remission (ICMR STW).
Monitor sexual dysfunction, sedation, weight (ICMR STW).

teaching.scope: Anxiety disorders and OCD in Indian primary and district care.
learningObjectives: Identify the type of anxiety disorder.
Start and titrate escitalopram; limit benzodiazepines.
keyPoints: Escitalopram 5 mg, then 10 mg, then 20 mg.
CBT is preferred at tertiary level.

patientEducation: Explain anxiety and that physical symptoms are not dangerous.
SSRIs take weeks to work; early side effects settle.
lifestyleAndDiet: Reduce caffeine and alcohol; regular exercise and sleep.
